question: A farm started with 166 animals. They removed 95 animals for market. They added 64 animals from breeding. They added 66 animals from purchase. They multiplied by 8 to calculate feed cost. There were 32 wild animals (not counted). How much feed budget was needed?

A store had 223 items initially. They removed 69 items for the morning sale. They removed 75 more items in afternoon. They added 67 items from new delivery. They multiplied by 9 for inventory calculation. They divided by 6 to split between locations. They multiplied by 9 again for the final count. How many items was the final count?

A factory started with 161 units. They removed 5 units for inspection. They added 36 units from production. They multiplied by 4 for quality checks. They multiplied by 5 for the batch. They multiplied by 9 for annual projection. How many units were in the annual projection?

A school had 123 students. They added 48 students in week one. They added 16 students in week two. They added 57 students in week three. They added 68 students in week four. They divided by 2 to split into cohorts. There was 1 student council president (not counted). How many students per cohort?

A garden had 156 plants. They tripled by propagation. They removed 40 plants for transplant. They removed 355 more plants for landscaping. They multiplied by 7 for the growth calculation. They added 3 plants from cuttings. Tom had 18 plants and Linda had 25 plants. How many plants was the growth calculation?

A farm had 153 crops. They added 48 crops from spring planting. They removed 118 crops for harvest. They removed 24 more crops from disease. They multiplied by 7 for yield calculation. They removed 200 kilograms for market. They multiplied by 5 for annual projection. How many kilograms was the annual projection?

A gardener had 179 seeds. They added 32 seeds of type one. They added 3 seeds of type two. They multiplied by 3 for germination rate. They added 29 seeds that sprouted. How many sprouted seeds were growing?

A sports team had 72 balls initially. They added 8 balls from new equipment. They added 5 more balls from donations. They multiplied by 5 for storage calculation. They added 44 balls to each storage bin. They added 9 more volleyballs. They divided by 2 to split across courts. How many balls were at each court?

A factory had 169 products. They multiplied by 6 for packaging cost. They removed 929 dollars in expenses. They multiplied by 4 for quarterly planning. They added 42 units from bonus production. They multiplied by 7 for the half-year calculation. They multiplied by 9 for annual projection. How many was the annual projection?

A gym had 135 machines. They divided by 5 to organize into zones. They multiplied by 9 for usage scheduling. They added 20 machines for each zone. They multiplied by 5 to calculate maintenance hours. They added 18 hours for emergencies. There were 12 stationary bikes (not counted). How many maintenance hours were needed?

A business had 232 orders. They added 54 orders in the morning. They removed 98 orders after fulfillment. They multiplied by 3 to calculate processing time. They added 33 hours for customer service. How many processing hours were allocated?

A store had 124 items. They added 41 items from delivery. They multiplied by 3 for inventory calculation. They multiplied by 4 to determine shelf space. They added 67 items from donations. They multiplied by 6 for the expansion plan. How many items was the expansion plan?

A farm had 239 animals. They removed 14 animals for market. They multiplied by 9 to calculate feed amount. They added 21 animals from breeding. They removed 857 kilograms of grain purchased. How many kilograms of grain were needed?

A library had 227 books to process. They added 34 books from donations. They added 57 books from purchases. They added 4 more books from returns. They removed 222 books for archiving. How many books remained to catalog?

A bakery had 233 items. They added 20 items from morning prep. They multiplied by 5 for the daily batch. They added 37 items from afternoon bake. They added 52 items from the delivery. How many items were in inventory?

A school had 171 textbooks. They added 31 textbooks for new courses. They added 12 more textbooks from purchase. They multiplied by 4 to determine number of copies. They removed 97 textbooks for recycling. How many textbooks remained in use?

A restaurant had 226 meals. They removed 93 meals from lunch service. They multiplied by 5 to calculate daily production. They added 17 meals for special orders. They multiplied by 9 to get weekly total. They added 72 meals from catering. How many meals were needed weekly?

A builder had 63 materials. They removed 27 materials for the foundation. They removed 17 materials for framing. They removed 7 materials for roofing. They divided by 2 to calculate per-house needs. How many materials per house?

A warehouse had 155 boxes. They divided by 5 for organizing into sections. They added 31 boxes to each section. They removed 16 boxes for the first shipment. They removed 23 boxes for the second shipment. There were 8 damaged boxes (not counted). How many usable boxes remained?

A store had 102 products. They removed 57 products from clearance. They added 34 products from new stock. They multiplied by 4 to calculate value. They added 14 more products from returns. There were 12 seasonal items (not counted). How much was the product value?

A company had 220 files. They added 20 files from new documents. They divided by 4 to organize into categories. They added 34 files to the first category. They divided by 2 to split tasks. How many files per task?

A musician had 193 songs. They multiplied by 9 to calculate practice time. They added 45 songs from new compositions. They added 16 songs from collaborations. They added 35 songs from remixes. How many hours of practice time?

A library had 202 books initially. They added 77 books from donation. They multiplied by 6 for the catalog value. They added 77 books from purchase. They removed 824 books for archive (in dollars). They multiplied by 6 for insurance calculation. How many dollars was the insurance value?

A student had 118 dollars. They removed 113 dollars for textbooks. They multiplied by 9 to calculate semester budget. They added 48 dollars from part-time work. They removed 92 dollars for supplies. There was a 25-dollar grant (not used). How much was the semester budget?

A factory produced 62 units. They multiplied by 4 for the shift calculation. They multiplied by 9 for the batch size. They divided by 6 to split quality checks. They divided by 3 for three inspectors. How many units did each inspector check?
